data_issues.Issue: Rows that follow a gap of more than one month within a carrier-route series
data_issues.Interpretation: Unbalanced-panel continuity issue affecting 19,240 training series
data_issues.RecommendedTreatment: Create lag/rolling features only when exact prior periods exist; preserve missing-history indicators.

key_findings.Evidence: 316,490 of 1,882,779 carrier-route-month rows (16.81%) do not have an exact observed next-month target. These rows are excluded from supervised modeling rather than imputed.
In training, target mean is 5,048.63, median is 2,479.00, and skewness is 3.46. mean/median gap and skewness quantify demand asymmetry.
Passengers has largest absolute Pearson correlation with next-month target (0.977).
Average next-month demand is highest in Oct (5,538.9) and lowest in Jan (4,303.1) in training partition.
lowest aggregate training demand occurs in 2020-04, with 2,858,797 target passengers, showing a material time-regime shock.
55,165 training observations follow a gap longer than one month in their carrier-route series, so future lag/rolling features must enforce exact calendar continuity.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Preserve chronological month-based split and never randomly shuffle observations across time.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: project predicts future demand; temporal leakage would inflate validation/test performance.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Do not impute missing target values; exclude rows for which exact next-month outcome is unavailable.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: supervised outcome is unknown, not merely a missing predictor.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Fit all predictor imputation, encoding, scaling, and transformation rules on training data only.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: Using validation/test distributions to design preprocessing leaks information from future periods.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Represent carrier/origin/destination categorical information with a modeling-appropriate encoding learned from training data.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: These are high-cardinality identifiers and cannot be passed as raw strings to most regression estimators.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Consider log1p target modeling, robust losses, or tree-based models rather than deleting legitimate high-volume routes as outliers.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: Route-month passenger demand is expected to be strongly right-skewed and operational extremes may be genuine rather than errors.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Engineer lags/rolling features only from information available at or before forecast origin, with explicit gap handling.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: carrier-route panel is unbalanced; naive shift/rolling operations can silently bridge missing months.

preprocessing_recommendations.Recommendation: Consider calendar seasonality and a pandemic/regime indicator during feature engineering/model comparison.
preprocessing_recommendations.Rationale: time series spans materially different demand regimes and seasonal patterns.
